const answer = `IDEA: BRad-RQ
TITLE: Behaviour-ranked radial Poincare assignment: training-transition context entropy sets each item's hyperbolic radius, curvature sets the quantizer score
MOTIVATION: An RQ-VAE SID prefix is currently a purely semantic token. Nothing in the quantizer forces the coarse prefix to correlate with how generic or context-specific an item is, so the Stage3 generator must learn prefix popularity structure implicitly from short histories. If the first SID level is stratified by a measured, training-only generality statistic, the coarse prefix becomes a cheaply predictable "how generic is this item" token and the later levels only refine the angle (fine semantics), which should raise prefix predictability and Stage3 Recall@10.
NOVELTY: Earlier mechanisms here put behaviour into the quantizer cost (successor mass in a Poincare Sinkhorn cost), into the codebook update (successor-weighted Poincare Frechet means), into the curvature itself (per-level curvature from hard prefix hit rate), into a cone/boost/Lorentz-profile/fibre variant, i.e. behaviour always modifies a weight, a curvature, a mean or a translation. Here behaviour modifies the RADIAL COORDINATE of the item point only (a rank map of a measured entropy statistic), the curvature is fixed at c = 1 and therefore can never be saturated by a protective bound, and the geometry acts in the nearest-codeword score through the Poincare factor 1/((1-|a|^2)(1-|e|^2)), which is exactly what makes radial matching dominate for far items and angular matching dominate for near items. No Sinkhorn, no Frechet update, no cone, no translation, no per-level curvature, no auxiliary loss.
CHANGE: Replace the encoder magnitude by a behaviour-derived rank radius, r_i = artanh(0.9 * rank(s_i)/(N+1)), send the item to the Poincare point p_i = exp_0(r_i * z_i/|z_i|), and choose each RQ level's codeword by argmin of the Poincare distance between exp_0(residual) and exp_0(squashed codeword) instead of the Euclidean distance, while the reconstruction/commitment losses stay Euclidean on the same tangent target t_i = r_i * z_i/|z_i|.
SPECIFICATION: (1) Precompute, from training sequences only, C[j,i] = directed co-occurrence counts of consecutive items, n_i = sum_j C[j,i], p_ji = C[j,i]/n_i, H_i = -sum_j p_ji log p_ji, s_i = (n_i*exp(H_i) + 1*sbar)/(n_i+1) with sbar = mean{exp(H_i) : n_i >= 10} and s_i = sbar for items never observed. (2) rank_i = rank of s_i over the N = 24556 training items (ties by item id), u_i = rank_i/(N+1) in (0,1), rho_i = 0.9*u_i, r_i = artanh(rho_i) in (0, 1.4722). (3) Per step: zhat = z/max(|z|,1e-8), t = r_i*zhat, u = t; for l = 1..L: a = u * min(1, 0.9/max(|u|,1e-8)), e_lk = tanh(|m_lk|)*m_lk/|m_lk| with m_lk the level-l tangent codebook after squash min(1,0.9/|m_lk|), score s_lk = |a - e_lk|^2 / ((1-|a|^2)(1-|e_lk|^2)), k_l = argmin_k s_lk, u = u - m_lk; t_hat = sum_l m_lk_l; loss = |t - t_hat|^2 + beta|t - sg[t_hat]|^2 + |sg[t] - t_hat|^2 with the baseline beta; emit SID(i) = (k_1,...,k_L). (4) Curvature c = 1 is derived, not tuned: after direction normalisation |zhat| = 1 so the unit tangent scale is the encoder scale, giving ball radius 1/sqrt(c) = 1 and no scale mismatch. All other constants are the documented defaults 0.9 (boundary margin), 1 (Laplace prior count) and the baseline beta.
COST: One extra pre-training pass over the training transition stream (O(E), a sparse COO count of a few million entries, tens of seconds, CPU, done once and cached as a length-N float vector); no extra parameters, no extra epochs, no extra forward pass. Per step at the frozen scale (batch 1024 = 24556/24, L = 3, K = 256, d = 64): 786432 distance evaluations, about 1.6e8 flops, i.e. roughly one extra elementwise pass over the similarity tensor the baseline already forms, under 1 percent of a step and under 2 percent of an epoch wall-clock.
HYPOTHESIS: For the idea to be worth keeping, the stability of the level-1 prefix with respect to the behaviour statistic must be real: the level-1 codeword radius must track r_i, so that level-1 prefix ids are nearly monotone in rho_i and the mean r_i of the items sharing a level-1 prefix separates strongly across prefixes; and the level-1 prefix must become more predictable from the same history because it now carries a popularity/generality prior. Observable as a high Spearman correlation between level-1 prefix index and the mean r_i of its items, a drop in level-1 conditional entropy of the prefix given the previous item on training transitions (diagnostic only), and, the judgement, Stage3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 from the single frozen run.
RISKS: Discarding the encoder magnitude may cost reconstruction, because magnitude previously carried some frequency information that the residual cascade now has to rebuild from radius; the hyperbolic score may let level-1 codewords collapse onto radial bands and waste angular capacity, so level 2 and 3 do all the semantic work; the rank map makes the radii uniformly spread, which overweights the tail relative to the head; the residual norm clamp at 0.9 may bind at levels 2 and 3 and waste capacity on badly reconstructed items; and Stage3 may already model popularity from the history, in which case a popularity-stratified prefix adds nothing and Recall stays flat.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Behaviour-conditioned context generality: the effective number of distinct predecessor contexts of an item, exp(H_i), from directed item-to-item transitions in the training split, equivalently a popularity-adjusted in-neighbour statistic because the entropy is taken over the predecessor distribution and therefore normalises out raw popularity.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: Count directed consecutive-item pairs (S_t -> S_{t+1}) over every training sequence, build the sparse count matrix C, take n_i = sum_j C[j,i] and p_ji = C[j,i]/n_i, compute H_i = -sum_j p_ji log p_ji over observed predecessors, convert to s_i = exp(H_i), shrink towards the measured prior sbar = mean{exp(H_i) : n_i >= 10} with weight 1/(n_i+1), assign s_i = sbar to items absent from the training transitions, then rank-normalise s_i over the 24556 training items and map to r_i. Computed once, offline, before Stage 2, and stored as a fixed buffer.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: The statistic reads only training-split sequences; C, sbar, the ranks and r_i are frozen before any Stage 2 or Stage 3 optimisation, no validation or test interaction is touched, validation/test items never contribute counts, and items without training transitions get the frozen prior sbar instead of any inferred value, so no test-time signal can reach the SID construction.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Fixed negative curvature c = 1 (derived from the unit-norm direction normalisation), Poincare exponential map exp_0(v) = tanh(|v|) v/|v|, and the Poincare distance in its monotone squared form s(x,y) = |x-y|^2 / ((1-|x|^2)(1-|y|^2)) whose arcosh is the geodesic distance.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: In the quantizer, at every RQ level, inside the nearest-codeword assignment: the codeword is chosen by the curved score between the exponential image of the current tangent residual and the exponential image of the codeword, and the item's point itself is produced by exp_0 of the behaviour-radius tangent vector.
COUPLING PATH: The behaviour rank sets the tangent norm r_i, the tangent norm is the argument of exp_0, its image p_i enters the Poincare score against exp_0(m_lk), and the argmin over that score fixes the SID token; the reconstruction target and the residual cascade then run on the same t_i = r_i zhat. Remove behaviour (r_i constant) and every item sits at one radius so the curved score can only separate angles; remove geometry (Euclidean score) and the radius still exists but the 1/((1-|a|^2)(1-|e|^2)) factor is gone so radial banding no longer dominates and the codeword choice changes.
COUPLING EQUATION: k_l(i) = argmin_k s_P( exp_0( clamp(t_i - sum_{j<l} m_{j k_j(i)}, 0.9) ), exp_0( squash(m_lk) ) ), with t_i = artanh(0.9 * rank(s_i)/(N+1)) * z_i/|z_i| where s_i is the behaviour context-entropy statistic and s_P is the fixed-curvature (c = 1) Poincare squared-distance kernel.
OBSERVABLES: Level-1 prefix ids become nearly monotone in rho_i (high Spearman between prefix index and mean r_i of its members); the within-prefix spread of r_i shrinks compared with the behaviour-off arm; level-1 conditional entropy of the prefix given the previous item on training transitions drops; codebook usage at level 1 concentrates in radially separated bands; the reconstruction loss on the same target t is compared with the geometry-off arm; and finally Stage3 test_recall@10, single run, above 0.065.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: rho_i = 0.45 for every item (the median of the rank map, i.e. all items at one radius r = artanh(0.45) = 0.4847, tangent target t_i = 0.4847 * zhat_i); curvature and the Poincare score unchanged, so only the behaviour-driven radial separation is removed.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: Same behaviour radii r_i and the same tangent target t_i, but the score is the Euclidean |a - e_lk|^2 and exp_0 is the identity, so codewords are plain bounded Euclidean points and the radial-matching pressure of the curvature disappears.
ABLATION BOTH ON: The full coupled run: r_i from the behaviour rank map, exp_0 into the ball, Poincare score for every level, Euclidean reconstruction on t_i.
SPEC EQUATIONS: Offline: C[j,i] += 1 per consecutive training pair; n_i = sum_j C[j,i]; p_ji = C[j,i]/n_i; H_i = -sum_j p_ji log p_ji; s_i = (n_i exp(H_i) + sbar)/(n_i + 1); sbar = mean{exp(H_i) : n_i >= 10}; s_i = sbar if n_i = 0; u_i = rank(s_i)/(N+1); rho_i = 0.9 u_i; r_i = 0.5 log((1+rho_i)/(1-rho_i)). Online per step: zhat = z/max(|z|,1e-8); t = r_i * zhat; u = t; for l in 1..L: a = u * min(1, 0.9/max(|u|,1e-8)); m = m_l * min(1, 0.9/|m_l|); e = tanh(|m|) * m/|m|; s_lk = |a - e_lk|^2/((1-|a|^2)(1-|e_lk|^2)); k_l = argmin_k s_lk; u = u - m_l[k_l]; t_hat = sum_l m_l[k_l]; L_total = |t - t_hat|^2 + beta |t - sg(t_hat)|^2 + |sg(t) - t_hat|^2; SID(i) = (k_1,...,k_L).
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: encoder output z in R^d for the batch (d = 64), the frozen per-item radius buffer r in R^N, the L tangent codebooks m_l in R^{K x d} (L = 3, K = 256), the switch flags behaviour_on and geometry_on. Outputs: per-item SID tuple (k_1,...,k_L), the tangent reconstruction t_hat, and the scalar loss; the codebooks, the encoder and the item radii are the only state that reaches Stage 3 (radii are frozen, codebooks are read only through the emitted SIDs).
SAFEGUARDS: Normalise the direction with max(|z|, 1e-8); keep rho_i in (0, 0.9) so 1 - rho_i^2 >= 0.19 and the Poincare denominator can never vanish (the margin 0.9 is a documented boundary default, and it is applied to the input rank map BEFORE artanh, exactly the normalise-first rule, so no protective cap ever truncates the behaviour statistic: the whole rank range 0..1 maps monotonically into 0..0.9 and the applied radius 0..1.4722); clamp tangent norms at 0.9 with min(1, 0.9/|v|) instead of division by a possibly zero norm, using max(|v|,1e-8); compute the score through s = |a-e|^2/((1-|a|^2)(1-|e|^2)) and never through arcosh, so no arcosh domain error; add 1e-12 to the denominator; freeze the radius buffer (requires_grad = False) so no gradient can drift it into the boundary; leave items without training transitions at the frozen prior sbar.
END IDEA`;

HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Fixed negative curvature c = 1 (derived from the unit-norm direction normalisation), Poincare exponential map exp_0(v) = tanh(|v|) v/|v|, and the Poincare distance in monotonically transformed squared form s(x,y) = |x-y|^2/((1-|x|^2)(1-|y|^2)), whose arcosh is the geodesic distance.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: In the quantizer, at every RQ level, inside the nearest-codeword assignment: the codeword is chosen by the curved score between the exponential image of the current tangent residual and the exponential image of the codeword, and the item point itself is produced by exp_0 of the behaviour-radius tangent vector.
COUPLING PATH: The behaviour rank sets the tangent norm r_i, that norm is the argument of exp_0, its image p_i enters the Poincare score against exp_0(m_lk), and the argmin over that score fixes the SID token; the reconstruction target and the residual cascade then run on the same t_i = r_i*zhat. Remove behaviour (r_i constant) and every item sits at one radius so the curved score can only separate angles; remove geometry (Euclidean score) and the radius still exists but the 1/((1-|a|^2)(1-|e|^2)) factor is gone, so radial banding no longer dominates and the codeword choice changes.
COUPLING EQUATION: k_l(i) = argmin_k s_P( exp_0( clamp(t_i - sum_{j<l} m_{j k_j(i)}, 0.9) ), exp_0( squash(m_lk) ) ) with t_i = artanh(0.9 * rank(s_i)/(N+1)) * z_i/|z_i|, where s_i is the behaviour context-entropy statistic and s_P is the fixed-curvature (c = 1) Poincare squared-distance kernel.
OBSERVABLES: Level-1 prefix ids nearly monotone in rho_i (high Spearman between prefix index and mean r_i of members); within-prefix spread of r_i shrinks versus the behaviour-off arm; level-1 conditional entropy of the prefix given the previous item drops; level-1 codebook usage concentrates in radially separated bands; reconstruction loss on the same target t compared with the geometry-off arm; and finally Stage3 test_recall@10 from one frozen run, above 0.065.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: rho_i = 0.45 for every item (median of the rank map, one radius r = artanh(0.45) = 0.4847, tangent target t_i = 0.4847*zhat_i); curvature and the Poincare score unchanged, so only the behaviour-driven radial separation is removed.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: Same behaviour radii r_i and same tangent target t_i, but score is Euclidean |a-e_lk|^2 and exp_0 is the identity, so codewords are plain bounded Euclidean points and the radial-matching pressure of the curvature disappears.
ABLATION BOTH ON: The full coupled run: r_i from the behaviour rank map, exp_0 into the ball, Poincare score at every level, Euclidean reconstruction on t_i.
SPEC EQUATIONS: Offline: C[j,i] += 1 per consecutive training pair; n_i = sum_j C[j,i]; p_ji = C[j,i]/n_i; H_i = -sum_j p_ji log p_ji; s_i = (n_i exp(H_i) + sbar)/(n_i+1); sbar = mean{exp(H_i) : n_i >= 10}; s_i = sbar if n_i = 0; u_i = rank(s_i)/(N+1); rho_i = 0.9 u_i; r_i = 0.5 log((1+rho_i)/(1-rho_i)). Online per step: zhat = z/max(|z|,1e-8); t = r_i*zhat; u = t; for l in 1..L: a = u*min(1, 0.9/max(|u|,1e-8)); m = m_l*min(1, 0.9/|m_l|); e = tanh(|m|)*m/|m|; s_lk = |a-e_lk|^2/((1-|a|^2)(1-|e_lk|^2)); k_l = argmin_k s_lk; u = u - m_l[k_l]; t_hat = sum_l m_l[k_l]; L_total = |t-t_hat|^2 + beta|t-sg(t_hat)|^2 + |sg(t)-t_hat|^2; SID(i) = (k_1,...,k_L).
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: encoder output z in R^d for the batch (d = 64), frozen per-item radius buffer r in R^N, L tangent codebooks m_l in R^{K x d} (L = 3, K = 256), flags behaviour_on and geometry_on. Outputs: per-item SID tuple (k_1,...,k_L), tangent reconstruction t_hat, scalar loss; the only state reaching Stage 3 is the emitted SIDs (radii frozen, codebooks read only through the SIDs).
SAFEGUARDS: Normalise direction with max(|z|,1e-8); keep rho_i in (0,0.9) so 1-rho_i^2 >= 0.19 and the Poincare denominator never vanishes (the 0.9 margin is applied to the INPUT rank map before artanh, the normalise-first rule, so no protective cap truncates the behaviour statistic: the full rank range 0..1 maps monotonically into 0..0.9 and radius 0..1.4722); clamp tangent norms with min(1, 0.9/|v|) and max(|v|,1e-8) instead of dividing by a possibly zero norm; evaluate the score via s = |a-e|^2/((1-|a|^2)(1-|e|^2)) and never via arcosh, avoiding domain errors; add 1e-12 to the denominator; keep the radius buffer requires_grad = False so no gradient drifts it into the boundary; leave items without training transitions at the frozen prior sbar.
END IDEA
